questions.q: What did Yahweh tell Ezekiel to present and speak to the house of Israel?
questions.a: Yahweh told Ezekiel to present a riddle and speak a parable to the house of Israel.

questions.q: In the parable, where did the large eagle plant the tips of the cedar tree branches?
questions.a: The large eagle planted the tips of the cedar tree branches in the land of Canaan in a city of merchants.

questions.q: In the parable, where did the large eagle plant the seed of the land, and how did it grow?
questions.a: The large eagle planted the seed beside a large body of water, and the vine produced branches and sent out shoots.

questions.q: In the parable, what did the vine do when the other great eagle came?
questions.a: The vine turned its roots towards the other great eagle.

questions.q: What did Yahweh say would happen to the vine in the parable?
questions.a: Yahweh said that the vine would completely wither away in its plot.

questions.q: What did the king of Babylon do with the king of Jerusalem?
questions.a: The king of Babylon took the king of Jerusalem to Babylon.

questions.q: What did the king of Babylon do with the royal descendant of the king of Jerusalem?
questions.a: The king of Babylon made a covenant with the royal descendant of the king of Jerusalem.

questions.q: How did Yahweh say the land of Israel would survive?
questions.a: Yahweh said the land of Israel would survive by the king of Jerusalem keeping his covenant with the king of Babylon.

questions.q: How did the king of Jerusalem violate the covenant he made with the king of Babylon?
questions.a: The king of Jerusalem rebelled and sent ambassadors to Egypt to acquire horses and an army.

questions.q: What did Yahweh say would happen to the king of Jerusalem?
questions.a: Yahweh said the king of Jerusalem would die in the middle of Babylon.

questions.q: According to Yahweh, whose covenant did the king of Jerusalem actually break?
questions.a: According to Yahweh, the king of Jerusalem actually broke his covenant with Yahweh.

questions.q: What did Yahweh declare would happen to the armies of the king of Jerusalem?
questions.a: Yahweh declared the armies of the king of Jerusalem would fall by the sword.

questions.q: What did Yahweh say he would do with the tender branches of the cedar tree?
questions.a: Yahweh said he would plant the tender branches on a high mountain.

questions.q: What will the tender branches that Yahweh plants become?
questions.a: The tender branches Yahweh plants will become a majestic cedar where every winged bird will live.

commentary.text: A parable relative to the Jewish nation. (Ezek. 17:1-10) to which an explanation is added. (Ezek. 17:11-21) A direct promise of the Messiah. (Ezek. 17:22-24)

Ezek. 17:1-10 Mighty conquerors are aptly likened to birds or beasts of prey, but their destructive passions are overruled to forward God's designs. Those who depart from God, only vary their crimes by changing one carnal confidence for another, and never will prosper.

Ezek. 17:11-21 The parable is explained, and the particulars of the history of the Jewish nation at that time may be traced. Zedekiah had been ungrateful to his benefactor, which is a sin against God. In every solemn oath, God is appealed to as a witness of the sincerity of him that swears. Truth is a debt owing to all men. If the professors of the true religion deal treacherously with those of a false religion, their profession makes their sin the worse; and God will the more surely and severely punish it. The Lord will not hold those guiltless who take his name in vain; and no man shall escape the righteous judgment of God who dies under unrepented guilt.

Ezek. 17:22-24 The unbelief of man shall not make the promise of God of none effect. The parable of a tree, used in the threatening, is here presented in the promise. It appears only applicable to Jesus, the Son of David, the Messiah of God. The kingdom of Satan, which has borne so long, so large a sway, shall be broken, and the kingdom of Christ, which was looked upon with contempt, shall be established. Blessed be God, our Redeemer is seen even by the ends of the earth. We may find refuge from the wrath to come, and from every enemy and danger, under his shadow; and believers are fruitful in him.
